General.Description:
The city of Hartwell has been declared a Red Zone. Armed insurgents have locked down six city blocks, cut communications, and taken three hundred civilians hostage inside the Hartwell Convention Centre. Negotiators are stalled. Special units are twenty minutes out. And Detective Sergeant Ray Moran is already inside.

What begins as an off-duty coffee break becomes the most gruelling fight of Moran's career as he navigates the siege from the inside — room by room, floor by floor — attempting to keep hostages alive while identifying the insurgents' true objective. Because this is not a ransom demand. It is a distraction.

Connor Blake delivers a masterclass in confined-space tension. Red Zone unfolds in real time over a single terrifying afternoon, drawing readers deeper into a labyrinthine building where every corridor may be the last and every decision carries lethal consequence.

Moran is a detective, not a soldier. He has no tactical gear, no backup, and no margin for error. What he does have is an intimate knowledge of human behaviour under extreme pressure — and a stubborn refusal to let the body count rise on his watch.

Brutal, breathless, and impossible to put down.
